---
title: "Install MISP 3.0 on Red Hat Enterprise Linux"
---

This guide installs the latest [MISP `3.0_wip` branch](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/tree/3.0_wip) on a clean Red Hat Enterprise Linux server.
It uses Apache with PHP-FPM, MariaDB, a local Redis-compatible service, and Supervisor.
The examples use `/var/www/MISP` and the distribution's `apache` account.
On Fedora, use the [Fedora Server installation guide](../install-fedora/index.qmd).

::: {.callout-note}
`3.0_wip` is the MISP 3.0 development branch. Evaluate it on a disposable host before deploying it.
The experimental `xINSTALL.rhel94.sh` in that branch installs MISP 2.5. Use the manual 3.0 steps below. [RHEL script source](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/blob/3.0_wip/INSTALL/xINSTALL.rhel94.sh)
:::

The package and application checks used Rocky Linux 9 and AlmaLinux 10 containers with the daemons started directly.
Validate subscription access, systemd startup, and SELinux enforcement on a registered RHEL test host.

## Choose your RHEL packages {#rhel-install-packages}

Use a current RHEL 9 minor release with the PHP 8.3 stream available, or a current RHEL 10 release.
PHP 8.3 was introduced in RHEL 9.6.
MISP 3.0 requires MariaDB 10.11 or later for this database path. [RHEL 9.6 release notes](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/9/html/9.6_release_notes/new-features) · [MISP database requirements](../requirements/index.qmd#software-requirements)

::: {.table-responsive}

| Component | RHEL 9.6 or later in the 9 series | RHEL 10 |
|---|---|---|
| PHP | AppStream `php:8.3` module stream | PHP 8.3 RPM packages |
| MariaDB | AppStream `mariadb:10.11` module stream | `mariadb-server` RPM package |
| Cache and queues | `redis` and `redis.service` | `valkey` and `valkey.service` |
| Web service | `httpd` and `php-fpm` | `httpd` and `php-fpm` |

:::

MISP connects to Valkey through the PHP Redis extension and the same Redis protocol and settings.
See the package changes and database instructions from Red Hat. [RHEL 9 MariaDB](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/9/html/configuring_and_using_database_servers/using-mariadb_configuring-and-using-database-servers) · [RHEL 10 MariaDB](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/html/configuring_and_using_database_servers/using-mariadb) · [RHEL 10 Valkey](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/html/considerations_in_adopting_rhel_10/infrastructure-services)

Start with a registered RHEL server that has BaseOS and AppStream enabled.
Use a `sudo` account, a DNS name, and a trusted TLS certificate and key for that name.
Keep web access limited to your administration network until the bootstrap password is changed.

Enable CodeReady Linux Builder and the matching EPEL repository through your organization’s approved repository configuration.
EPEL supplies packages used below, including Supervisor and the fuzzy-hash development library.
For a Red Hat Subscription Management host with direct access to Fedora EPEL, use the following. [EPEL setup for RHEL](https://docs.fedoraproject.org/en-US/epel/getting-started/)

```bash
rhel_major=$(rpm -E '%{rhel}')
sudo subscription-manager repos \
  --enable="codeready-builder-for-rhel-${rhel_major}-$(arch)-rpms"
sudo dnf install \
  "https://dl.fedoraproject.org/pub/epel/epel-release-latest-${rhel_major}.noarch.rpm"
sudo dnf repolist
```

On **RHEL 9**, select the MariaDB and PHP streams first, then install MariaDB and Redis.

```bash
sudo dnf module enable mariadb:10.11 php:8.3
sudo dnf install mariadb-server redis
```

On **RHEL 10**, install MariaDB and Valkey.

```bash
sudo dnf install mariadb-server valkey
```

On **both releases**, install the common packages and check the PHP client extensions.

```bash
sudo dnf install git curl ca-certificates openssl unzip file-libs procps-ng iproute \
  httpd mod_ssl php-cli php-fpm php-mysqlnd php-mbstring php-xml \
  php-gd php-intl php-bcmath php-pecl-zip php-pecl-redis6 \
  python3.12 python3.12-pip python3.12-devel gcc ssdeep-devel \
  policycoreutils-python-utils supervisor
php --version
php --ri redis
php --ri pdo_mysql
mariadb --version
```

Ensure the PHP Redis RPM is available for the installed PHP stream.
If your approved repositories do not provide a matching RPM, have your package administrator supply one built for that PHP version before continuing. [PHP Redis package for EPEL 9](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/php-pecl-redis6/php-pecl-redis6/)

## Install MISP and its dependencies {#rhel-install-source}

Install Composer with the verified installer procedure and make its executable available as `/usr/local/bin/composer`.
Use the signed or checksum-verified download procedure from Composer. [Composer installation and verification](https://getcomposer.org/download/)

Clone the latest `3.0_wip` branch and the submodules selected by that branch.

```bash
sudo install -d -o apache -g apache -m 0755 /var/www/MISP
sudo -u apache git clone --branch 3.0_wip --recurse-submodules \
  https://github.com/MISP/MISP.git /var/www/MISP
sudo -u apache git -C /var/www/MISP status --short --branch
sudo -u apache git -C /var/www/MISP rev-parse HEAD
```

Use a private directory for application data and Composer's state, then install the dependencies for the checkout.

```bash
sudo install -d -o apache -g apache -m 0750 /var/lib/misp \
  /var/lib/misp/composer /var/lib/misp/attachments
sudo -u apache env COMPOSER_HOME=/var/lib/misp/composer \
  /usr/local/bin/composer --working-dir=/var/www/MISP/app \
  install --no-dev --no-interaction --prefer-dist
sudo -u apache env COMPOSER_HOME=/var/lib/misp/composer \
  /usr/local/bin/composer --working-dir=/var/www/MISP/app \
  check-platform-reqs --no-dev
sudo -u apache python3.12 -m venv /var/www/MISP/venv
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python -m pip install \
  -r /var/www/MISP/requirements.txt
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python -m pip check
```

## Initialize the database and local services {#rhel-install-database}

Before starting MariaDB, set `bind-address=127.0.0.1` in a `[mariadb]` section in `/etc/my.cnf.d/misp.cnf`.
Keep Redis or Valkey bound to loopback as well.
Use `systemctl cat redis.service` on RHEL 9 or `systemctl cat valkey.service` on RHEL 10 to locate the service's configuration.
Start MariaDB and whichever cache service you installed.

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now mariadb
# RHEL 9
sudo systemctl enable --now redis
redis-cli ping
# RHEL 10
sudo systemctl enable --now valkey
valkey-cli ping
```

The selected cache client should return `PONG`.
Open a local MariaDB administrator session with history disabled for the credential setup.

```bash
sudo env MYSQL_HISTFILE=/dev/null mariadb
```

Use the following SQL for a new database.
Replace the example password with a unique secret and retain it for the application configuration.

```sql
CREATE DATABASE misp
    CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci;
CREATE USER 'misp'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'REPLACE_WITH_DATABASE_PASSWORD';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON misp.* TO 'misp'@'localhost';
EXIT;
```

Load the MariaDB schema from the same checkout and copy the branch's application configuration templates.

```bash
sudo mariadb misp < /var/www/MISP/INSTALL/MARIADB.sql

for config_name in bootstrap core database config; do
  sudo install -o apache -g apache -m 0640 \
    "/var/www/MISP/app/Config/${config_name}.default.php" \
    "/var/www/MISP/app/Config/${config_name}.php"
done
```

Edit `/var/www/MISP/app/Config/database.php` with `sudoedit`.
Set the default connection's `login` to `misp` and `password` to the database password.
Keep `host` set to `localhost` for the local socket and `database` set to `misp`.

Edit the corresponding keys inside the `MISP` section of `/var/www/MISP/app/Config/config.php`.

```php
'baseurl' => 'https://misp.example.org',
'external_baseurl' => 'https://misp.example.org',
'osuser' => 'apache',
'org' => 'Your organization',
'python_bin' => '/var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python',
'attachments_dir' => '/var/lib/misp/attachments',
'redis_host' => '127.0.0.1',
'background_jobs' => false,
```

Use your DNS name and organization.
Keep the default Redis port `6379`.
Before creating the administrator, generate a unique instance salt with `openssl rand -hex 32` and set `Security.salt` to that value in the same configuration file.
Keep it private and include the file in instance backups.
Start with jobs disabled while loading the schema and creating the bootstrap administrator.
Run the application commands as `apache`.

```bash
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin runUpdates
sudo sh -c 'umask 077
runuser -u apache -- /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake User init \
  > /root/misp-bootstrap-api-key'
sudo -u apache /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin schemaDiagnostics
```

Confirm that the schema reports `Pending: 0` and `Failed: 0`.
Protect the generated bootstrap API key.

## Configure SELinux and serve HTTPS {#rhel-install-web}

Keep SELinux enforcing.
Give Apache write access to application configuration, runtime files, and attachment storage with persistent file contexts.
The script workspace under `app/files/scripts/tmp` must also be writable for temporary files created by MISP.
The rest of the checkout uses the read-only web content type from the standard `/var/www` policy.

```bash
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_rw_content_t \
  '/var/www/MISP/app/(Config|tmp)(/.*)?'
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_rw_content_t \
  '/var/www/MISP/app/files/scripts/tmp(/.*)?'
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_content_t '/var/lib/misp'
sudo semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_sys_rw_content_t \
  '/var/lib/misp/attachments(/.*)?'
sudo restorecon -F /var/lib/misp
sudo restorecon -RF /var/www/MISP /var/lib/misp/attachments
sudo setsebool -P httpd_can_network_connect_db on
sudo setsebool -P httpd_can_network_connect on
```

The database boolean permits the web runtime to access MariaDB.
The network boolean permits web requests to reach Redis or Valkey and the Supervisor API over TCP, and also permits other outbound web-process connections.
Apply your site's network policy to the services MISP should access.
For access errors, inspect SELinux denials and the labeled paths. [Red Hat SELinux documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/html/using_selinux/index)

Use the distribution's Apache PHP-FPM configuration and the `apache` PHP-FPM pool.
In `/etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf`, replace the example TLS virtual host block with the following and keep the global TLS settings, including `Listen 443 https`.
Use your real hostname and paths to the certificate chain and private key.

```apache
<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName misp.example.org
    DocumentRoot /var/www/MISP/app/webroot
    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /etc/pki/tls/certs/misp-fullchain.pem
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/pki/tls/private/misp.key

    <Directory /var/www/MISP/app/webroot>
        Options -Indexes
        AllowOverride FileInfo
        Require all granted
        DirectoryIndex index.php
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>
```

MISP's `app/webroot/.htaccess` sets the rewrite and authorization rules.
Check `httpd -M` for `rewrite_module`, `headers_module` and `proxy_fcgi_module`.
Check that the FPM pool listens on `/run/php-fpm/www.sock` and permits access by `apache`. [Apache and PHP-FPM on RHEL 10](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10/html/installing_and_using_dynamic_programming_languages/using-the-php-scripting-language)

```bash
sudo restorecon -v /etc/pki/tls/certs/misp-fullchain.pem \
  /etc/pki/tls/private/misp.key
sudo php-fpm -t
sudo httpd -t
sudo systemctl enable --now php-fpm httpd
```

If your host uses firewalld, check `sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones` and allow the `https` service in the zone restricted to administration traffic during setup.
Verify the HTTPS certificate and sign in from the restricted administration network.
The first account is `admin@admin.test` with password `admin`.
Change it on the first login before granting other clients access.

## Start the background workers {#rhel-install-workers}

Enable Supervisor's authenticated HTTP API on loopback.
Add or update the following section in `/etc/supervisord.conf`.
Use a separate secret for the Supervisor password and restrict the file to root.

```ini
[inet_http_server]
port=127.0.0.1:9001
username=supervisor
password=REPLACE_WITH_SUPERVISOR_PASSWORD
```

Create `/etc/supervisord.d/misp-workers.ini` with one process per job queue and a separate scheduler process.

```bash
{
  printf '%s\n' '[group:misp-workers]' \
    'programs=default,email,cache,prio,update,scheduler'
  for worker in default email cache prio update scheduler; do
    if [ "$worker" = scheduler ]; then
      cake_command=scheduler_worker
    else
      cake_command="start_worker $worker"
    fi
    cat <<EOF

[program:$worker]
command=/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake $cake_command
directory=/var/www/MISP
user=apache
autostart=true
autorestart=true
redirect_stderr=true
stdout_logfile=/var/www/MISP/app/tmp/logs/$worker-worker.log
EOF
  done
} | sudo tee /etc/supervisord.d/misp-workers.ini > /dev/null
```

In the `SimpleBackgroundJobs` section of `app/Config/config.php`, set `redis_host` and `supervisor_host` to `127.0.0.1`.
Keep Supervisor's port `9001` and set `supervisor_user` and `supervisor_password` to match `supervisord.conf`.
Set `MISP.background_jobs` to `true` and start Supervisor.

```bash
sudo chmod 0600 /etc/supervisord.conf
sudo systemctl enable --now supervisord
sudo supervisorctl status 'misp-workers:*'
```

All six processes should report `RUNNING`.
Check the worker and queue status in the MISP administration interface and verify that a background job completes. [Background worker checks](../administration/index.qmd#admin-background-jobs)

## Verify the installation and plan upgrades {#rhel-install-check}

- Check `ss -lnt` for your HTTPS listener and confirm that the database, cache and Supervisor listeners use loopback.
- Verify the certificate, sign-in and redirects from a client that trusts your CA. Save and search for an unpublished, organization-only test event.
- Confirm the site organization, distribution defaults, mail settings, and the administrator API key. Check backup and restore before enabling sync or scheduled feeds. [First steps after login](../quick-start/index.qmd#first-steps-after-login)

For an existing MISP 2.5 instance, follow the [offline database upgrade](../upgrade-2-5-to-3-0/index.qmd) for backups, staging and validation.
On RHEL, run Cake commands as `apache`, use the RHEL service names, and run `sudo systemctl restart php-fpm` after the migration.
Rehearse on a restored copy to measure the database and maintenance window.
